evidence.field: 形義通解；就 的字形與早期用例
evidence.text: The database reports that oracle-bone and bronze forms of 就 are composed of 亯 and 京, interpreted as a temple form placed above a high platform, with the proposed sense ‘sacrifice at a high place.’ It says Chu forms share strokes between 亯 and 京, while the Qin slips first show the form 京 + 尤 that informed small-seal 就. It distinguishes early uses: oracle-bone examples are mostly place names; a Western Zhou inscriptional phrase 申就乃命 uses 就 verbally with a sense near ‘complete’; bronze examples also include travel uses, including 就郢 on the Warring States 鄂君啟車節. These are source analyses, not an uncontested chronology of all senses.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫：就

evidence.source: 復旦大學出土文獻與古文字研究中心；陳致
evidence.field: 金文、甲骨文與早期語義討論
evidence.text: The article reviews competing readings of early forms. It notes that most oracle-bone cases with the 亯 + 京 form are place names and are not attested as verbs in those contexts; it discusses the interpretation of an oracle-bone case as 就庸 as an earlier scholarly proposal. It identifies a mid-Western Zhou 史惠鼎 example in 日就月將, while discussing whether the phrase means continued increase/progress or has a ritual reading. Its author argues that the old graphic form included 亯 + high/京 + 止 and that later 又/尤 forms reflect graphic corruption of 止; the article also presents the alternative that Warring States 就 can be borrowed for 造 in travel contexts. This makes the identification of every early graph with the later verb and the explanation of the lower component disputed.
evidence.kind: scholarly paleographic argument with explicit competing analyses
evidence.title: 陳致：“日居月諸”與“日就月將”：早期四言詩與祭祀禮辭釋例

evidence.field: 就 entry
evidence.text: Xu Shen’s Eastern Han dictionary defines 就 as ‘high’ and analyzes it as 从京从尤, explaining 尤 as ‘different from the ordinary’; it also records 𡰜 as a Zhou-script form. This is an important historical account but does not by itself establish that the earliest graphic form had 尤 or that 尤 was originally the phonetic element.

evidence.field: 形義通解；京 entry
evidence.text: The database analyzes archaic 京 as depicting a tall platform or tower, with its original sense ‘large/high platform’; it reports later uses for place names and the capital, and cites the Shuowen definition ‘a very high mound made by people.’ 京 is thus an independently semantic element in the earliest proposed 就 graphic analysis, not evidence for the later component’s sound role.

evidence.field: 形義通解；尤 entry
evidence.text: The database reports a bronze form of 尤 as 又 plus a small extra mark, interpreted by cited scholars as a hand bearing a growth; it gives the proposed original sense ‘wart/lump’ and extensions including ‘unusual’ and ‘especially.’ It also reproduces the Shuowen analysis of 尤 as ‘different’ and 又 as phonetic. These descriptions make semantic motivation for the Shuowen explanation intelligible, but they do not establish that 尤 was the lower component in the earliest 就 graph.

evidence.field: Old Chinese reconstruction table, v1.1 (2014), entries 尤 and 就
evidence.text: In the Baxter–Sagart 2014 system, 尤 yóu is Middle Chinese hjuw and Old Chinese *[ɢ]ʷə; 就 jiù is Middle Chinese dzjuwH and Old Chinese *[dz]u[k]-s, glossed ‘go to.’ The authors describe their MC column as a notation for Middle Chinese source data, not itself a reconstruction. gaps: The precise identification and semantic value of the earliest oracle-bone 亯 + 京 examples remain disputed: available sources report them mostly as place names and record an older proposed verb interpretation, but do not settle whether they represent 就 in the later verbal sense.

A direct semantic development from ‘high’/‘sacrifice on a high place’ to verbal senses such as ‘complete’ or ‘go to/approach’ is not established by the inspected evidence. The early attested uses are distinct and should not be arranged as a simple dictionary-gloss chronology.

The lower element in the earliest graphic is unsettled: sources variously describe 尤 in the Qin/small-seal form, a prior 止 element with later graphic confusion, and an early pictographic/semantic 亯 + 京 formation. Consequently, a secure phonetic role for 尤 in the earliest 就 is not established. Baxter–Sagart entries give 尤 *[ɢ]ʷə versus 就 *[dz]u[k]-s; local rows for 京 and 就 preserve their exact notation, and do not establish 尤 as a matching phonetic.

The role of 京 in the later formation is reported as semantic in Shuowen, but the early 亯 + 京 graph analysis assigns 京 a graphic/semantic role in the ‘high platform’ scene rather than identifying the whole graph as an ordinary phono-semantic compound.

Official Unicode Unihan character-specific URLs for U+4EAC, U+5C31 and U+5C24 were attempted but inaccessible to the web tool. Local exact reading rows were checked, and accessible nonofficial mirror pages were inspected; the requested official per-character click-through verification remains a limitation.
